## Week 5: Who counts as a case

Every dataset has a rule for who gets into it: who was born small, who was hired, who answered the survey, who was released on bail. When that rule depends on two things at once, looking only at the people it let in creates an association between those two things that is not there in the population. Colliders on a causal graph; a model that leaves out a sensitive attribute and becomes both less accurate and more unequal between groups; data missing completely at random, at random, and not at random; what dropping the incomplete rows does to an estimate, and what filling them in assumes.

**Required reading:** [Hernán and Robins, Causal Inference: What If, chapter 8: Selection bias](https://miguelhernan.org/whatifbook) (Chapman and Hall/CRC, 2020; free online version of 21 November 2025; sections 8.1 to 8.5, pages 109 to 121) · re-read [Barocas, Hardt and Narayanan, Fairness and Machine Learning, chapter 5: Causality](https://fairmlbook.org/pdf/fairmlbook.pdf) (the subsection "Colliders", pages 112 and 113, and the list of what controlling for each kind of variable does, page 115)

**Optional:** [van Buuren, Flexible Imputation of Missing Data](https://stefvanbuuren.name/fimd/ch-introduction.html) (second edition, 2018; sections 1.1 to 1.3, for the names missing completely at random, at random, and not at random) · [Elwert and Winship, Endogenous Selection Bias: The Problem of Conditioning on a Collider Variable](https://users.ssc.wisc.edu/~elwert/causality/wp-content/uploads/2014/07/Elwert-Winship-2014.pdf) (*Annual Review of Sociology*, 2014; section 4, and the examples of truncation, nonresponse and attrition in section 5) · [Lakkaraju, Kleinberg, Leskovec, Ludwig and Mullainathan, The Selective Labels Problem](https://cs.stanford.edu/~jure/pubs/contraction-kdd17.pdf) (KDD 2017; section 1) · [van Buuren, section 2.7: When not to use multiple imputation](https://stefvanbuuren.name/fimd/sec-when.html) · [Hernández-Díaz, Schisterman and Hernán, The birth weight "paradox" uncovered?](https://doi.org/10.1093/aje/kwj275) (*American Journal of Epidemiology*, 2006)

**Bring to the class:** one dataset or study where some people who should be in it are not, with who is missing and in which direction their absence pushes the result.
